description: The right gloved hand holds a white trigger spray bottle at the front of the hood. No label is visible. The spray nozzle is aimed at the open left palm, and the glove surface looks wet. The left hand closes into a fist after spraying while the right hand still holds the bottle. The gloved hands are pressed together, rubbing. The hands keep rubbing together, and the bottle has been put down. The reagent concentration is not readable.

Side bench: a clear glass PBS bottle and a pink orange-capped bottle sit beside the microscope, and the operator holds the spray bottle. Wiping with a paper wipe. A bottle labelled 'TC CMF PBS' sits in the background and a small white-cap bottle is in hand. The pink orange-capped bottle is held and wiped. A white-cap 'gibco 1X' bottle and the PBS bottle are on the bench. 'TC CMF PBS' label readable on the glass bottle. The pink bottle and the gibco 1X bottle are next to it. The operator carries the pink medium bottle and the gibco 1X bottle toward the hood. These frames do not establish the reagent identities.

The operator holds the white spray bottle at the side bench next to the PBS bottle and the pink medium bottle. The operator handles a white paper wipe taken from the hood's top tray. The right hand wipes the neck and cap of the orange-capped medium bottle while the left hand holds the gibco 1X bottle. The medium bottle is held up and turned; the wipe is seen against the bottle. The medium bottle and the gibco 1X bottle are carried to the hood opening. The frames do not establish whether the wipe was wetted with ethanol.
